identity.fantasy: A living siege beetle that turns incoming blows into Rage, armor states, regeneration, poison pressure, and violent counterattacks.
identity.one_line: An exoskeleton tank built on Carapace regeneration, Chitin, poison retaliation, Impale, Expulsion, and Molt. It combines high self-repair with AoE poison threat. Recent community builds and discussion consistently identify it as one of the strongest-feeling current dungeon tanks, but that is observational rather than a verified ranking.

mechanics.core_loop: Let incoming attacks build Exposed Flesh, decide whether to clear those stacks through Expulsion, Regrow Exoskeleton, or another effect, maintain a safe amount of Carapace Regeneration, spread Venomtip Poison, and use Impale or kiting to control large packs.
mechanics.single_target: Cycle Exposed Flesh into mitigation or poison pressure, keep survival layers active, and use Barbed Stinger and later sustain effects on durable targets.
mechanics.aoe: Expulsion, Venomtip Poison, Impale, Toxic Expulsion, and Locust Swarm create strong area pressure that scales naturally with being attacked by many enemies.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Most survival state lives on the tank rather than one target; Impale lines, pack grouping, kiting, and Molt movement still require spatial control.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Carapace Regeneration, Regrow Exoskeleton, Reformed, Charm of Warding, Locust Swarm, and later regeneration talents create extensive self-sustain; Impale adds a long line stun.
mechanics.group_utility: Fortitude contributes grouping stability, attack-speed reduction, a line stun, and the ability to survive unusually large pulls while damage-over-time effects work.

failure_modes.text: Holding too many Exposed Flesh stacks or using all Carapace Regeneration charges carelessly can turn the spec's survival engine against itself.

Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: most survival state lives on the tank rather than one target; impale lines, pack grouping, kiting, and molt movement still require spatial control.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: carapace regeneration, regrow exoskeleton, reformed, charm of warding, locust swarm, and later regeneration talents create extensive self-sustain; impale adds a long line stun.

append_claims.text: A July player guide describes Fortitude as a high-self-healing, physical-damage-resistant AoE DoT tank; it recommends maintaining only one or two Carapace Regeneration stacks, clearing Exposed Flesh deliberately, using taunt for venom interactions, and lining packs for Impale.
append_claims.notes: Detailed single-author guide from the early-release environment.

append_claims.text: Several July tank players describe Fortitude as exceptionally durable with strong AoE damage in open-world and dungeon-style pulls.
append_claims.notes: Levels, gear, and pull sizes are not normalized.

append_claims.text: Fortitude's central skill test is deciding when Exposed Flesh should be converted into damage, mitigation, healing, or control rather than simply clearing it on cooldown.
